clue.text: One who sounds partial to a drink

indicators.note: the clue says the word only sounds like a partial person, so we want something said the same way

parts.note: someone partial, one who takes sides, is a sider

explanation.surface: Someone admits a fondness for a particular drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who ... partial' describes a biased person, a sider, and 'sounds' tells you the answer is pronounced the same but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is the fermented apple drink, a plain example of a drink.

clue.text: Field in Provence eradicated vipers entangled in scattered grape vines to produce this

definitions.text: Field in Provence eradicated vipers entangled in scattered grape vines to produce this

parts.note: champ is the French word for a field

indicators.note: the letters of the snakes are rooted out of the other phrase
the snakes' letters are mixed up among the vine letters, not in a neat run
the grape vines are strewn about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French farmer clears snakes from tangled vines to make a sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letters are scattered through the vines rather than in a run, so 'entangled in' and 'scattered' both signal mixing. The whole clue describes how the wine comes about.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparkling wine is made from grapes grown in vineyards in a region of France, so the whole clue paints its making.

clue.text: By end of Diwali start to dye stolen fabric

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of the word dye

parts.note: stolen goods are said to be hot

indicators.note: the end of the word Diwali is its last letter, placed by the rest

explanation.surface: At the close of the Hindu festival someone starts to dye cloth that was stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By end of Diwali' puts the final I beside the rest, at the end: D, then HOT, then I.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the long cloth wrapped round the waist by Hindu men, so it is a length of fabric.

clue.text: Adjustment of minute rule for required length of computer program

indicators.note: an adjustment changes the arrangement of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Someone tweaks a rule about the minute, as if fixing regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Run time is the time a program takes to execute, so it is how long the software needs.

clue.text: Nun's time to embrace libation

parts.note: a Clare is a nun of the order of Poor Clares; the 's is a link
to cup is to hold in curved hands, a kind of embrace

explanation.surface: A nun reaches the moment to accept a drink offering.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Clares are a Franciscan order of nuns, so a Clare is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret cup is an iced punch of red wine with brandy and sugar, a drink, which a libation loosely is.

clue.text: Good health might be the response to periphery

definitions.text: Good health might be the response to periphery

parts.words: Good health might be the response to periphery
parts.note: the drinks that are answers round the edge of the grid would each draw a toast

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that wishing good health answers something on the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'periphery' is the outside of this grid, where the answers are all drinks; the natural response to a drink is the toast.
explanation.definitionFit: The toast said when raising a glass means good health to those drinking.

clue.text: Crashing into rear in front

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: One car smashes into the back of another, the one in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into rear' hints at the back; the answer means the opposite, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior is the anatomical and formal word for situated at the front.

clue.text: Type of web that's a money trap

parts.note: the euro is a currency, so money
a net is used to trap things

explanation.surface: A web that catches cash, as if the internet were a money trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Euronet was a European computer network, a kind of web of linked computers.

clue.text: Capable parent's not fit to flop around one dropping off

indicators.note: the letters of the word for fit are not included in the result
flopping around jumbles the remaining letters of the phrase

parts.note: fit means able

explanation.surface: A capable parent is too tired to function and flops about.
explanation.walkthrough: From CAPABLE PARENT take away ABLE ('not fit') and rearrange what is left ('to flop around').
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes a short sleep is dozing, dropping off for a moment.

clue.text: Place beside edge of park to plump down

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
on can mean beside, as a house on the river

indicators.note: the edge here is the final letter of the word park

explanation.surface: Someone sets themselves down heavily by the side of a park.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk something is to put it down heavily, as one plumps down onto a sofa.

clue.text: Soldier accepts uniquely modern decoration

indicators.note: one thing accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: done in a unique way, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A soldier takes on a distinctly modern medal or ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is not the usual GI or OR but the soldier ant, a caste of ant that defends the colony.
explanation.definitionFit: An adornment is something added to beautify, which is what a decoration is.

clue.text: Proportion shown in essential section of speech

indicators.note: the essential section of a word is its core, losing the first and last letters

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A proportion appears in the key part of a speech, perhaps a statistic quoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential section of' strips the outer O and N from ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses one quantity relative to another, which is a proportion.

clue.text: Parking right here in Paris, close to Seine river, is more expensive

parts.note: ici is French for here

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, of the word Seine

explanation.surface: Parking in central Paris by the Seine costs more.
explanation.definitionFit: Pricier is the comparative of pricey, costing more money.

clue.text: Quickly proceeded to plunder and pillage

parts.note: to go quickly is to run, past tense ran
to sack a town is to plunder it

explanation.surface: Raiders hurried off to loot and pillage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search thoroughly and rob, the same as to pillage.

clue.text: Became sticky with face turned to the sea

indicators.note: turning a word round reads it backwards

parts.note: mug is slang for face
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone's face turned towards the sea became sticky, perhaps with salt spray.
explanation.definitionFit: To gum is to become clogged or sticky, so the past tense means it became sticky.

clue.text: Runner seems green, energies depleted after exertions

indicators.note: depleted means the energy is used up, so its letter is taken out
after a lot of effort the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A runner looks pale and drained after hard training.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEMS GREEN has one E too many: 'energies depleted' removes it and 'after exertions' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner in the old sense carries messages from place to place.

clue.text: Unorthodox fighter in corrupt ring. What's up?

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped, so O

explanation.surface: A boxer in a crooked fight asks what is happening.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ring' looks like the boxing ring; it is the letter O, mixed with WHATSUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, whose stance is unorthodox.

clue.text: Daily whet? It's a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone's daily appetiser turns out to be a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' is both the mixing signal and, with the whole clue, a description of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A white lady is a cocktail of gin, orange liqueur and lemon juice, fit for a daily aperitif.

clue.text: Core of Dali's painting out in the open

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letters, of the name Dali

parts.note: a fresco is a painting done on wet plaster

explanation.surface: The centrepiece of a Dali exhibition is displayed outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco, from Italian, describes something done outdoors, in the fresh air.

clue.text: Performing, without aid of US, European men's blues group

indicators.note: performing puts the letters into action in a new arrangement
the letters of the word US are to be done without

explanation.surface: A European men's blues band plays without American help.
explanation.walkthrough: Take U and S ('without aid of US') from E plus MENSBLUES and rearrange the rest ('Performing').
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a group of musicians who perform together.

clue.text: Singer's party includes miraculous food? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: one thing including another holds it inside
this swaps the roles: the food holds the party, not the party the food

parts.note: manna was the food sent from heaven to the Israelites
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A singer's party includes a feast fit for a miracle, or rather the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is the American pop singer, one well-known example.

clue.text: In Italy police initiate summons before I take wife back

indicators.note: the summons letter comes before the rest
to initiate is to begin, so the first letter of the word summons
back means the words I take wife are read in reverse

parts.note: R, from Latin recipe, means take
rib refers to Eve, made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: Italian police start a summons before someone takes their wife home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IRRIB into BIRRI; R stands for take as on a prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: Sbirri is the Italian, sometimes derogatory, word for policemen, the plural of sbirro.

clue.text: Educate British in dog rearing

indicators.note: a rearing animal goes up, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: a pug is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Teaching the British about raising dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a child is to raise and educate them.

clue.text: Style of hat to wear in the country

explanation.surface: A hat to wear out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The hats actually come from Ecuador, not the country they are named after.
explanation.definitionFit: The straw hat and the Central American state share one name.

clue.text: Poet's a consumer

explanation.surface: A poet is just a consumer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender wrote poetry, and anyone who spends is a consumer.

clue.text: In the end always eat so you get fat

indicators.note: the end of each of the following words, so their last letters

explanation.surface: Eat all the time and you will grow fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means plump or heavily built, a polite word for fat.

clue.text: Idiotic like one in pub a touch ebriated

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: one is placed in the pub, inside its letters

parts.note: an inn is a pub
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a touch of a word is just its first letter, of ebriated

explanation.surface: Someone acting foolishly like a slightly tipsy drinker in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pub a touch ebriated' plays on inebriated, since 'in pub' itself supplies IN-I-N.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine, from the Latin for ass, means stupid or foolish.

clue.text: Less friendly pair dismissed from 11

indicators.note: the letters are sent out of the other word

parts.note: refers to the answer to 11-across

explanation.surface: A pair sent off by eleven players, which feels unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cricket or football team; it points to 11-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy describes a cold, unfriendly manner, so the comparative means colder and less warm.

clue.text: Vital part of newspaper?

definitions.meaning: a heart or liver is a vital part of the body
a party or group's official paper, its mouthpiece

explanation.surface: Is the newspaper a crucial component of something?
explanation.definitionFit: The body part and the publication that speaks for an organisation share the word.

clue.text: Sharing out half of territory in Hilton paradise

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order
half of a four-letter word for territory, its first two letters

parts.note: land is territory

explanation.surface: Splitting up land in a Hilton hotel heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hilton' looks like the hotel chain; it is James Hilton, whose novel Lost Horizon created the paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the imaginary Himalayan utopia in James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon.

clue.text: Sailor's 26 potentially a Spanish red

parts.note: a tar is a sailor; the 's is a link

indicators.note: the letters could potentially become something else, so rearrange them

parts.note: refers to the answer to 26-across

explanation.surface: A sailor's instrument might be a Spanish red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a Catalan region and port giving its name to a red wine.

clue.text: At SW19 did Fred serve this?

definitions.text: At SW19 did Fred serve this?

parts.words: At SW19 did Fred serve this?
parts.note: SW19 is the Wimbledon postcode; Fred ... won Wimbledon, and serve suggests both tennis and pouring a drink

explanation.surface: A question whether a tennis player served drinks at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: SW19 is the London postcode of Wimbledon. Fred Perry, the last British men's champion before 2013, shares his surname with the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry is a drink fermented from pears, the sort of thing one might serve.
